title: Finite type of a Noetherian subring detected by a universal submersion
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $E$ a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $R\subset E$ a $k$-subalgebra. Suppose that $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and that $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is universally submersive: for every commutative $R$-algebra $L$, the continuous map $\operatorname{Spec}(E\otimes_RL)\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is surjective and a subset of its target is open if and only if its inverse image is open. Then $R$ is finitely generated as a $k$-algebra. No finiteness of $E$ as an $R$-module is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, printed pp.31--32: take S=Spec k, X=Spec E and Y=Spec R. Read online arXiv:1005.2398v3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: First prove an auxiliary integral case: let $B$ be a Noetherian integral domain over $k$, let $C$ be a finite type $k$-algebra, and let $B\to C$ be any $k$-algebra map whose spectrum map $f:X=\operatorname{Spec}C\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is universally submersive. Injectivity of $B\to C$ will not be used. For the affine target $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, testing universal submersivity on algebra base changes suffices: on every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}L$ of a base scheme, the pullback is $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_B L)$; surjectivity and detection of open subsets are local on that affine cover. The same finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $C$ generates it over $B$, so $f$ is finite type; it is quasi-separated because its diagonal is the closed immersion induced by the surjection $C\otimes_B C\to C$, $c\otimes d\mapsto cd$. The generic-flatness-and-presentation lemma gives a nonempty open $U\subseteq Y$ on which $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Shrink $U$ to a nonempty principal open $D(s)$; this is affine, so quasi-compact by the affine qcqs lemma. That lemma also supplies the required qcqs property of $Y$. Apply admissible flattening to obtain a finite-type ideal $I\subseteq B$, with $I\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_U$, and a blowup $b:T=\operatorname{Bl}_IY\to Y$ such that the scheme-theoretic strict transform $q:X^{\prime}\to T$ is flat and of finite presentation. All quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hypotheses of flattening hold for the affine $Y$ and $f$.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, proof, printed pp.31--32 (read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S6.SS2)

proof.text: The ideal $I$ is nonzero since it restricts to the unit ideal on the nonempty $U$. Choose nonzero generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of $I$ (discard zero generators). The integral-blowup lemma gives that $T$ is integral. The blowup chart cover identifies its affine charts as $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, where $B_i=B[I/f_i]=B[f_1/f_i,\ldots,f_r/f_i]\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}B$. This equality follows from the definition of the chart algebra and the chosen ideal generators. Each $B_i$ is finite type over the Noetherian ring $B$, hence Noetherian. The finite affine cover is quasi-compact by the affine qcqs lemma, and its chart rings are Noetherian; thus $T$ is a Noetherian scheme. Also $b^{-1}U$ is nonempty open (the blowup is the identity on the admissible open) and hence dense in the integral $T$.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, proof, printed pp.31--32 (read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S6.SS2)

proof.text: The projection $g:X\times_Y T\to T$ is finite type by base change. It is universally submersive: every further base change is already a base change of $f$. Put $V=Y\setminus V(I)$. Since $I\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_U$, one has $U\subseteq V$. The strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure of the open pullback over $V$, so its closed support $|X^{\prime}|\subseteq|X\times_Y T|$ contains $g^{-1}(b^{-1}V)$ and hence $g^{-1}(b^{-1}U)$. This distinguishes the chosen flat open $U$ from the possibly larger complement $V$ of the blowup centre. Apply the closed-horizontal-support lemma with target $T$, dense open $b^{-1}U$, and closed subset $|X^{\prime}|$. Its hypotheses were verified in steps 1--2, so it gives that $q:X^{\prime}\to T$ is surjective. This uses only support containment; it does not replace the scheme-theoretic strict transform by a reduced topological closure.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, proof, printed pp.31--32 (read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S6.SS2)

proof.text: For each blowup chart, $X^{\prime}_i=X^{\prime}\times_T\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_B B_i)$, hence affine with coordinate ring a quotient of $C\otimes_B B_i$. The latter is generated as a $C$-algebra by the $r$ ratios $1\otimes f_j/f_i$; it is therefore a quotient of $C[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$. Consequently the finitely many $X^{\prime}_i$ are finite type over $k$, and their union $X^{\prime}$ is locally of finite type over $k$. Now $q$ is flat, locally finitely presented and surjective. Source descent of local finite type applied to $X^{\prime}\xrightarrow{q}T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives that $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. The affine-pair criterion then implies that every $B_i$ is a finite type $k$-algebra.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, proof, printed pp.31--32 (read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S6.SS2)

proof.text: For each $i$, choose finitely many $k$-algebra generators $c_{i\ell}$ of $B_i$. Because $B_i=B[f_j/f_i]$, each $c_{i\ell}$ is a polynomial in the ratios $f_j/f_i$ with finitely many coefficients from $B$. Let $A\subseteq B$ be the $k$-subalgebra generated by all these coefficients and all $f_j$, and put $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$. Then $A$ is finite type over $k$. For every $i$ the subring $A_i=A[J/f_i]\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}B$ is contained in $B_i$, but contains all $c_{i\ell}$ and $k$, so $A_i=B_i$. Here $A$ is a domain because it is a subring of $B$; the fractions used to define its charts thus embed in the same fraction field. The construction used finitely many coefficients and did not require $B$ to be module finite over $A$.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, proof, printed pp.31--32 (read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S6.SS2)

proof.text: Put $T_0=\operatorname{Bl}_J\operatorname{Spec}A$. The chart cover gives charts $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for $T_0$, equal to the charts $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of $T$. Use the affine-chart map into $D_+(f_i t)$ and the homogeneous localization overlap lemma. On the intersection of charts $i$ and $j$, both gluings use the subring $B_i[(f_j/f_i)^{-1}]=B_j[(f_i/f_j)^{-1}]$ of $\operatorname{Frac}B$, with the identity identification; these follow by inverting the respective homogeneous chart coordinates. Thus the chart identities glue to an isomorphism $T\simeq T_0$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. This argument identifies the map as well as the scheme: $T\to\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ restricts on chart $i$ to $A\hookrightarrow B_i=A_i$.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, proof, printed pp.31--32 (read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S6.SS2)

proof.text: The ring $A$ is Noetherian by finite-type permanence over the field $k$. Apply the projective-affine-base blowup lemma to the identity $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, which is H-projective via $\mathbf P^0_A$, and the finite-type ideal $J$. It makes $T_0\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ H-projective. Through the isomorphism in step 6, the composite $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is therefore H-projective. Each chart $A_i=B_i$ is Noetherian, so $T$ is locally Noetherian. Its structure sheaf is quasi-coherent of rank one, hence coherent by the finite-type quasi-coherent criterion. Projective coherent finiteness, with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_T$ and $q=0$, now gives that $M=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ is a finite $A$-module.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, proof, printed pp.31--32 (read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S6.SS2)

proof.text: The pullback homomorphism $B\to M$ is injective: its restriction to any chart is the inclusion $B\hookrightarrow B_i\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}B$; the charts are nonempty because $f_i\ne0$ in the domain $B$. This is an $A$-linear injection. Since $A$ is Noetherian and $M$ is a finite $A$-module, the submodule finiteness lemma makes $B$ a finite $A$-module. Choose module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $B$ and algebra generators $a_1,\ldots,a_t$ of $A$ over $k$. The $k$-subalgebra $k[a_1,\ldots,a_t,b_1,\ldots,b_s]$ contains every sum $\sum_j u_jb_j$ with $u_j\in A$, so equals $B$. This proves the integral auxiliary case, without any injectivity assumption on the original $B\to C$.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, proof, printed pp.31--32 (read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S6.SS2)

proof.text: Return to the given $R\subseteq E$. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the quotient $B=R/\mathfrak p$ is a domain, and is Noetherian because its ideals lift to finitely generated ideals of $R$; $C=E/\mathfrak pE$ is a finite type $k$-algebra. Its map to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, since $E\otimes_R(R/\mathfrak p)=E/\mathfrak pE$, so it is universally submersive directly from the hypothesis. Apply the integral auxiliary case proved in steps 1--8: $R/\mathfrak p$ is finite type over $k$. No injection $R/\mathfrak p\hookrightarrow E/\mathfrak pE$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Theorem 6.2.1, proof, printed pp.31--32 (read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S6.SS2)

proof.text: Apply prime filtration to the finite $R$-module $R$. It gives a finite filtration $0=M_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_n=R$ with $M_i/M_{i-1}\simeq R/\mathfrak p_i$. Each $R/\mathfrak p_i$ is finite type over $k$ by step 9. Choose lifts in $R$ of finitely many algebra generators of every quotient, and let $D\subseteq R$ be the $k$-subalgebra they generate. Then $D$ is finite type over $k$ and $D\to R/\mathfrak p_i$ is surjective for every $i$, so each filtration quotient is cyclic as a $D$-module. Inductively lift its one generator to $M_i$ and append it to a finite generating set of $M_{i-1}$: subtraction of its $D$-multiple places any element in $M_{i-1}$. Thus $R$ is a finite $D$-module. The algebra generators of $D$, together with these module generators of $R$, generate $R$ as a $k$-algebra, by the same sum argument as step 8. The empty filtration gives $R=0$ and the same conclusion. This handles nonreduced rings and all irreducible components, and proves the item.

The q=0 coherent cohomology finiteness theorem bounds the global-sections module of the descended blowup.
Affineness supplies the qcqs hypotheses for flattening and quasi-compactness of the finite chart cover.
Canonical homogeneous localization overlaps justify gluing the identical blowup charts over the finitely generated coefficient subalgebra.
